title: Do Minimum Wages Help Workers in Poor and Low-Income Families?
discussion_signal: The post quotes the NBER paper's direct low-income-family result: minimum-wage increases are associated with adverse employment, hours, and earnings effects among initially employed low-wage workers in poor and low-income families. It also includes a methodological challenge about wage-threshold selection, firm relocation, and employment composition, preserving disagreement rather than presenting the result as uncontested.
linked_research_question: When minimum wages are intended to support poor families, how do hours, employment, earnings, prices, firm adjustment, household resources, and worker selection combine to determine who gains or loses?
limits: The post quotes selected abstract language and is not a peer review
The public challenge raises identification concerns without resolving them
The linked record does not measure prices, consumption, firm profits, relocation, or the best alternative policy in the same unit
